question: Which tissue layer inside a joint is primarily affected during rheumatoid arthritis?
explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition that specifically targets the synovium, causing inflammation and the growth of destructive tissue known as a pannus. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main role of the pannus in damaging an arthritic joint?

options.A: Stretching the surrounding ligaments until they snap
options.B: Releasing enzymes that erode cartilage and bone
options.C: Increasing the production of calcium in the bone marrow
options.D: Blocking the normal flow of synovial fluid entirely

explanation: The abnormal pannus tissue produces enzymes that actively break down both the joint cartilage and the underlying bone. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h1)

question: How long does morning stiffness typically last for someone with active rheumatoid arthritis?
explanation: Morning stiffness that lasts for more than an hour is a classic clinical sign that helps distinguish rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h2)

question: A patient presents with painful, swollen finger joints in both hands that appear in the exact same spots on the left and right sides. What pattern of joint involvement is this?
explanation: When multiple small joints on both sides of the body are affected in a matching pattern, it is called symmetrical polyarticular involvement. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which blood test is known to be specific for diagnosing rheumatoid arthritis early on?
explanation: Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies are specific to rheumatoid arthritis and often appear in blood tests before any joint damage shows up on an X-ray. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why are erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) tests ordered when evaluating for rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: To check if the patient has an active bacterial skin infection
options.B: To measure the overall level of inflammation in the body
options.C: To calculate the exact amount of remaining cartilage in the knee
options.D: To determine if the patient is allergic to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Both ESR and CRP levels rise when inflammation is present in the body, helping clinicians understand how active the disease currently is. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which group of medications is considered the cornerstone of treatment because they slow down the progression of rheumatoid arthritis?
explanation: DMARDs alter immune system activity to halt disease progression and prevent permanent joint damage, unlike medications that only relieve pain. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of prescribing corticosteroids during an acute flare-up of rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying immune system malfunction
options.B: To rebuild the lost cartilage inside the damaged knee joints
options.C: To provide rapid anti-inflammatory relief while waiting for long-term drugs to work
options.D: To permanently eliminate the need for physical therapy

explanation: Corticosteroids work quickly to calm severe inflammation, bridging the gap until slower-acting DMARDs can take full effect. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which nursing action is most appropriate when a patient has a painful, acutely swollen joint flare-up?

options.A: Applying cold packs to help reduce localized swelling
options.B: Encouraging heavy weightlifting to stretch the joint capsule
options.C: Massaging the joint vigorously with coarse salt
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake for twenty-four hours

explanation: Cold therapy constricts blood vessels and numbs the local area, which helps reduce acute swelling and pain during a flare. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h5)

question: A patient with hand involvement asks for advice on managing daily chores. What guidance should the nurse provide?

options.A: Perform all heavy scrubbing in one long session to get it finished quickly
options.B: Avoid all movement of the hands and wrists for the rest of the year
options.C: Soak the hands in freezing ice water every morning before attempting chores
options.D: Use larger joints and ergonomic assistive devices to protect small hand joints

explanation: Protecting vulnerable small joints by using larger joints and adaptive tools helps prevent deformities and saves energy during daily tasks. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h5)

question: What are the firm lumps that often form under the skin over bony pressure points in patients with rheumatoid arthritis called?
explanation: Rheumatoid nodules are firm swellings that frequently develop under the skin over pressure points like the elbows. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do patients with chronic rheumatoid arthritis have a higher risk for cardiovascular complications?

options.A: Systemic chronic inflammation damages and accelerates atherosclerosis in blood vessels
options.B: Blood pressure medications are strictly contraindicated for anyone with arthritis
options.C: Patients are completely forbidden from engaging in any form of walking
options.D: The heart muscle grows too large from pumping blood through stiffened joints

explanation: Ongoing systemic inflammation promotes blood vessel damage and plaque buildup, which increases the risk of heart disease. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h6)
